lead: A small publishing house in Sweden, made by people who love a good question.
intro: Telning Publishing House makes wordless picture books for children aged 0 to 7. Each story is coloured by the child, who then chooses how it ends. Behind the books is a small team of cognitive and behavioural scientists in Uppsala, Sweden. Every book and every gift is designed in Sweden by our team of scientists and illustrators, and printed close to you.

made.h2: How is a Telning book made?

steps.t: We start from what studies say about shared reading, wordless books and talking about feelings.
One line per picture: what we see, what the character feels, what changes. Then the fork with two endings.

steps.h: Made by a person, with AI tools
steps.t: Pictures are made by a person together with AI tools. A person checks every picture.
Real children, real crayons. We change what confuses, and we keep what starts a talk.
Drawings on the right-hand pages only, on uncoated paper made for pencils and crayons, printed to order close to you.

artStyle.lead: Scandinavian folk art style: gouache painting texture, dry-brush acrylic strokes and visible coloured pencil grain.
artStyle.intro: Our pictures and our products share one design language. You see it on our Story Walls, mugs, tote bags, postcards and greeting cards: friendly cats and dogs with big round eyes, folk flowers, leaves and berries, and simple shapes in a few warm colours.

tech.t: Flat, matte areas of colour that cover the paper, like opaque water-based paint.
A brush with very little paint drags over the surface and leaves broken, scratchy edges.
The fine tooth of the paper shows through, like a coloured pencil on rough paper.
Bold lines that bend gently and change a little in width. Nothing is drawn with a ruler.

roots.t: In Dalarna in the 1700s and 1800s, painters decorated wall hangings and furniture with the kurbits, a large stylised plant full of flowers.
“Rose painting” began in rural Norway in the 1700s: flowing flowers and scrolls on wooden bowls, chests and walls.
Farmhouses in Hälsingland, Sweden, have rooms painted in the 1700s and 1800s. They are on the UNESCO World Heritage List since 2012.
In the 1950s and 1960s, Scandinavian designers brought simple shapes, flat colour and a playful line to textiles, ceramics and picture books.

artStyle.paletteNote: Some designs use one colour only: dark blue, Persian red, black or dark green.
artStyle.honest: Pictures are made by a person together with AI tools, in this style, and a person checks every picture. The textures are part of the printed picture: our products are printed to order, not painted by hand.
artStyle.artAlt: A tall mustard cat with black patches holds a small folk-patterned teacup, with folk flowers, leaves and berries around it: an example of our art style.

items.t: We say what a book is, not what it will do. No big claims, no numbers from studies on a cover.
Pictures are made by a person together with AI tools. A person checks every picture.
A story card needs a first name and an age. Never a photo of a child. We delete what we do not need.
We write only when a book is out. No tracking, no cookies on this site.

name.t1: "Telning" is Swedish for a young shoot, a sapling. In older Swedish it also means a child.
name.t2: Telning Publishing House is a Swedish publishing house. Every book, Story Wall and gift is designed in Sweden by our team of scientists and illustrators, and made for you after you order.
